title: Bioluminescent Garden Shader Lab
description: A mystical garden scene where a translucent plant is illuminated by a magical lantern. The user manipulates custom shader parameters on both objects — controlling subsurface scattering intensity, light color wavelength, fresnel glow, distortion amplitude, and emission pulses — while a conservation law ensures total energy across all shader channels remains constant. Full undo/redo support tracks every parameter change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads DiffuseTransmissionPlant.glb and Lantern.glb using GLTFLoader. Place the lantern at (1.5, 0, 0) and the plant at (-1, 0, 0) on a dark ground plane. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2.5, 5) with OrbitControls. Add dim ambient light (0.1 intensity) so the scene relies on shader-driven illumination. Replace materials on both models with custom ShaderMaterial. The plant shader must have uniforms: uSubsurface (0-1), uFresnelPower (0.5-5), uDistortion (0-0.3), uAbsorptionColor (vec3), and uPulseSpeed (0-3). The lantern shader must have uniforms: uEmissionIntensity (0-2), uLightHue (0-1 mapped to HSL), uFlickerAmount (0-1), uCausticScale (0.5-5), and uGlowRadius (0.1-2). Implement a point light parented to the lantern whose color and intensity sync with uLightHue and uEmissionIntensity. Implement an energy conservation law: define totalEnergy = uSubsurface + uEmissionIntensity + uFresnelPower/5 + uFlickerAmount + uDistortion/0.3, clamped to exactly 2.0. When any slider increases, proportionally decrease the others to maintain the sum. Build a sidebar UI with labeled sliders for all 10 uniforms grouped under Plant Shaders and Lantern Shaders headers. Display a real-time energy bar showing current distribution. Implement an undo/redo system: each slider change pushes a snapshot of all 10 uniform values onto a history stack. Bind Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z for redo, also provide UI buttons. The plant vertex shader should apply sine-wave distortion using uDistortion and time. The plant fragment shader should compute subsurface scattering approximation using view-dot-light with uSubsurface and Fresnel rim using uFresnelPower. The lantern fragment shader should pulse emission using sin(time*uPulseSpeed)*uFlickerAmount and project caustic patterns scaled by uCausticScale. Animate uPulseSpeed to create a living glow effect. The interaction requires adjusting at least 10 parameters across both shaders while respecting the energy conservation constraint, with full undo/redo capability.
